emulator.name: ROM emulator
emulator.blurb: Play your own NES, SNES, GB, GBA or Mega Drive ROM.

swf-player.name: Flash SWF player
swf-player.blurb: Open a Flash .swf file without a plugin.

emulator.q1: Which consoles and files does it open?
emulator.a1: FC / NES (.nes), SFC / SNES (.sfc, .smc), Game Boy and Game Boy Color (.gb, .gbc), Game Boy Advance (.gba) and Mega Drive / Genesis (.md, .gen, .smd, .bin), or a .zip holding one of these.
emulator.a2: No. The file is read in this tab and handed to the emulator on this page. Only the emulator itself is downloaded.
emulator.q3: Why does it ask me to choose a console?
emulator.a3: SNES files have no fixed header, and a .bin or a zipped .bin can be anything. If the file does not name its console, pick one under Console and the game starts.
emulator.a4: No commercial ROMs. Open a file you have the right to use. The Games column has free homebrew that starts without a file.
emulator.q5: How do I play and save?
emulator.a5: The controls appear once a game starts. On a phone, use the on-screen pad; a Bluetooth gamepad works too. Save and load states from the emulator toolbar.

swf-player.q1: Do I need Adobe Flash Player?
swf-player.a1: No. Ruffle, an open-source Flash emulator, runs the file in the page. There is nothing to install.
swf-player.a2: No. The file stays in this tab and is not sent to a server.
swf-player.q3: Why does my SWF stop on a loading screen?
swf-player.a3: This page runs a file that can start on its own. It blocks network access, so a game that loads more SWFs, XML or its old website stops there.
swf-player.a4: Most older ActionScript 1 and 2 files do. ActionScript 3 support in Ruffle is still incomplete, so some newer games fail to start or misbehave.
swf-player.a5: Browsers block audio that plays by itself. Click the picture once and the sound starts.

swfPlayer.title: Flash SWF player
swfPlayer.privacyNote: Open a .swf file in this tab with Ruffle. No Flash plugin. Nothing is uploaded.

emulator.lead: Open your ROM and play on this page. Nothing is uploaded.
emulator.s1b: Press Choose ROM and pick a .nes, .sfc, .gb, .gbc, .gba, .md or .zip file.
emulator.s2b: The console is detected from the file. If it is wrong or unknown, choose one under Console and the game restarts.
emulator.s3b: Use the keys listed under the game, the on-screen pad on a phone, or a Bluetooth gamepad.

swf-player.lead: Open a .swf file in this tab with Ruffle. No plugin, nothing uploaded.
swf-player.s1b: Press Choose SWF and pick a .swf file. The file stays in this tab.
swf-player.s2b: It starts by itself. Click the picture once to turn on the sound.
swf-player.s3b: Most Flash files use the mouse; a tap on a phone is a click. Arrow keys work when the game expects a keyboard.
